title: How Adam Robinson used founder edutainment on LinkedIn to take RB2B from $1MM to $2MM ARR in six weeks
summary: Adam Robinson explains why he treats his company as an "edutainment" media brand with software at the bottom of the funnel. He covers writing for people with his own pain, saying the uncomfortable truth, building a warm audience above sales, using LinkedIn comments for networking, and bootstrapping to $10MM ARR.

principles.text: Run the company as an edutainment media brand; software sits at the bottom of the funnel.
principles.quote: I view myself in the edutainment business and I happen to sell SAS at the bottom of the funnel but like I'm not competing with my competitors on SAS and features

principles.text: Write for people who share your exact pain right now, not an audience you only serve.
principles.quote: What if I started writing to people who were basically me and not like writing to Shopify store owners

principles.text: Great content says what everyone feels but no one admits, including your own struggles.
principles.quote: when you say things that connect with people so deeply because they're feeling it and no one is willing to admit it to themselves like that's that's what I think makes great content

principles.text: Build the awareness layer above outbound; reps only capture warmth that content created.
principles.quote: what that rep's really doing is just capturing the machine of warmth that you created above it

principles.text: Treat website-visit leads as warm: filter to ICP and push them through every channel quickly.
principles.quote: of the leads that we would give you filter out the ICP leads throw away all the rest of them and just stick them into that tumbler

principles.text: Use LinkedIn comments to get known by the right people; a small targeted following is enough.
principles.quote: if you can just get in people's comments constantly like they they will know you after a few months
